reviews.comment: Lots of homework due in (seemingly) short amounts of time, very forgiving partial credit on exams. Very organized course for the summer.
Unhelpful regarding questions about assignments and frequently has errors in his notes/test reviews. Talks down to students and hypes himself up non-stop. Take Turkan.

Textbook reading will help you learn the best, do lots of practice problems. I was frustrated with the unreachability the professor had, and the strict late/turn-in policies. Start homework way ahead of time and prepare for turning things in quickly via pdf scan in class.

Mashuga is the worst professor I've had at TAMU. He skips theory and process, simply showing problems then jumping to answers. You're forced to self-teach everything. To make matters worse, he didn't post midterm grades until two hours before the Q-drop deadline. Avoid his class if you want a professor who actually explains the content.

Mashuga does not deserve all the hate he gets. He is very caring and really wants you to succeed. He gives good practice exams and puts together nice slides that most of the other professor do not do. His lectures are not the most engaging, but he does know the material well and answers questions if you need clarification.

There is very little difference between his lectures and having a audio book reader read out his slides. He doesn't even go through the problems in his slides (which have typos) in detail. Instead he just reads out these complex problems with hardly any explanation. Seems like a nice person, but a horrible lecturer.

Only go to lecture if you want to hear the most didn't happen stories and him bragging about everything he has every done. Inconsistent homework grading, and when I emailed him about it he said there's nothing he can do about it. $100-$200 textbook REQUIRED?? At least the exams were open note open book, but still hard.

Least accommodating professor of all time,refuses extension requests. No sympathy,never accessible,refuses to answer q's after class, inconsistent hw grading. Hard copy of textbook(upwards of $100)was required for the exam. Most lectures were useless other than test review,mostly bragged about the equipment he built and made rude,unfunny comments.

Absolute WORST professor I have ever had here. He genuinely did not care if his students succeeded and gave very few resources. He was hardly accessible outside of class. He literally sent a message to the entire class telling us to stop emailing him for anything. Often made rude comments or answered rudely to questions.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Very rude and passive aggressive towards students. Inaccessible outside of class and few resources given to succeed in the class. Office hours were appointment based only and rarely responded to emails.

The WORST prof I've had at A&M so far. This is the first class I've ever gotten a B in and it's in large part because of Dr. Mashuga. His lectures are him reading off cluttered slides that are not helpful. The homework took forever and the exams were overly difficult because he would often mess up the questions. Take ANYONE else.

DON'T TAKE I have had classes with rude and difficult professors before that I could get through with no problem, but Mashuga takes the cake. He is condescending to an abnormal degree. No basic respect given as he criticizes us for his mistakes. Anyone saying it's "part of college" is delusional. Is completely inaccessible outside AND inside class.

This professor was honestly horrendous. He was inaccessible, hated getting emails from students, and honestly just couldn't teach the class material. The second exam was worth about 20% of our grade and almost 70 points worth of it was completely messed up on the exam paper. Half the class q-dropped after the second exam. DO NOT PICK.

DO NOT TAKE. He is inaccessible out of class (ONLY appointment based office hours), dislikes getting emails from students, and unprepared for lecture/exam. Took no responsibility for forgetting to print compressibility chart and had typos/missing information he changed with 30 min left of the exam. Lectures consist of him clicking through slides.

Do not take! Lectures were Mashuga clicking through worked out slides with little explanation given. He never gave adequate answers to any questions and was condescending about it. He botched 65 pts of exam 2 and his idea of "fixing" it was giving the same exam AGAIN for 10 pts added to a failing average. Refused to curve even with failing averages

Going to his class ruined my whole day. His class takes drinking from a fire hose to a whole new level. Homework due soon? Get ready to put your life on hold to get it done. Oh wait, forget doing well even if you prepare because he didn't have reference material on the exams. Have a question about the material? Yeah, get ready to get chewed out.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Mashuga did a terrible job at preparing us for his overly difficult exams. He was unreachable by email and he constantly booked over his office hours so he was never available. The HW is nothing like the exams and they do nothing to prepare you for them. Mashuga has refused to curve despite the exam averages regularly being in the 50s. Worst Prof..

Class is terribly structured. Forced to complete homework and exam over material that hadn't been taught. Provided no key to the exam review he gave for the first exam. Few resources to study. Only reads off slides that get very messy quickly. Botched two exam questions on second exam and did little to address or fix. No curve even with F average.

Don't take. He completely disregards students in person and via email. Only way to succeed in class is to spend more hours in a week studying than the total hours he has spent this entire semester helping students through this course. OR, you could be lucky and be in the later section which doesn't suffer as much from butchered exams. Avoid.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: has unrealistic expectations for an introductory course - expected us to have the intuition of junior/senior chen students. read off disorganized and crammed slides and handed off duties to the co-instructor whenever possible. unclear grading criteria on exams and provided unhelpful reviews. answers for final exam review given the NIGHT BEFORE

Most inaccessible professor I have had, comes into his one hour office hours late and does not respond to emails. He is rude and aggressive when asked questions about specifics of the course and grades. He is extremely unprepared even though he has taught CHEN courses before. He avoids answering questions by telling stories of his past. AVOID HIM!!

This is the first time I have ever written a review on here (He is that bad). CHEN 204 is hard but he makes it worse. I get it's his first time teaching this class, but it's not his first time teaching. He never lets you finish talking and never actually answers your questions. You can tell he is only here for his research.

do not take. completely inaccessible outside of class; acts like students are bothering him when they ask questions, quite literally told us to stop emailing him. screwed up exam 2 to the point where it was unsolvable, did not take any responsibility, and only gave one opportunity for 10 "bonus" points to rectify a situation that was his fault.

Mashuga's exams were overly difficult, with no useful review materials. Homework was due before topics were taught, and one exam lacked correct data, with fixes given too late to complete. All sections received the same corrections, though only one had issues. He avoids accountability, directs students to TAs instead of offering help. DO NOT TAKE!!

Just no. His first time teaching this class which keep in mind is an INTRO class and after having exams of 60< and 50< averages decides to not curve and give 10 points keeping the average at at most a 60, while being adamant of never giving out a curve. Please stay away from this guy and ignore the ai generated people who are leaving good reviews.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had he is extremely caring if you care about his class first. He can come off as condescending, grow up, its college. His slides were good. Homework's were time consuming but relatively simple. He is great at making up for his mistakes, and while he wants you to learn the content he also cares about your grade

I'd take him again. So sue me. Even if he's not always prepared, it's his first time to ever teach the course. And he DID give 10 potential bonus points on an exam, let us redo a 40 point question from an exam, and even gives helpful hints on quizzes sometimes. It is an extremely hard class, but his caring personality certainly made it bearable.

Dr. Mashuga's 204 class was a poor experience. Exam averages were 58, with Exam 1 including content not in the syllabus. Exam 2 had errors and lacked a compressibility chart needed for a 40%-weighted problem. He missed two of the last three lectures, leaving the assistant professor to fill in, bonus points were poorly handled. Avoid this class.

This professor is inaccessible. He never responses to emails and always let the co-instructor or the graders to do that. People come to his office hours for help and what they got was 'Here is the answer. Work backwards.'. Not communicative on exam materials. Exam 1 and Exam 2 average are both 58. Don't take him!!

I normally do not review profs, but beware of taking 204 with Mashuga. He is unprepared, and he has made himself inaccessible outside of lecture. He does not keep his class timeline, and he makes no effort to accept fault when he makes errors that cost the class. If you can take anyone else for Chen 204, I would.

DO NOT TAKE CHAD. This professor is inadequate in many ways, has character flaws that make him impossible to like or trust. His interactions with students are full of passive-aggressive behavior and he is intentionally non-communicative on grade cutoffs/curves/distributions. Other review that says "15 points back on exam" is entirely not true, fyi.

There were two problems worth >60% of the exam that were riddled with errors and unsolvable. Lectures are full of jokes regarding stop signs, obscure bands, and drunk college roommates from Mashuga's youth. You are better of taking Ijaz Muhammed, the escaped walmart greeter, who lied on his resume to become a professor at A&M. Insane Grading.

Mashuga is tough, but fair. Mashuga is very reachable through email, office hours, and is online savvy. Even though he made a mistake on an exam, he made up for it by giving us 15 bonus points plus an exam replacement. He is going the extra mile to make sure people actually learn the material by slowing down on lectures and verbally walking us thru

CHEN204 is already tough, and having him as your professor won't help. He only meets by appointment and rushes through slides without explaining the problem-solving logic. His exams are unorganized and even has information missing. You'll end up self-studying most of the course. In short, DO NOT take his class; find a professor who cares.

He is unreachable outside of office hours and takes no accountability. 1st exam tested on material (bypass) that was not testable according to the syllabus. The 2nd exam was completely botched - 65% of it was impossible for our section to complete until 20 minutes left in class. In office hours, he told us "if you fail, you fail." Avoid this man.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mashuga is a nice man. His lectures and exams are not nice. Partial credit is given on exams, but grading criteria is unclear. Lectures involve reading off of slides rather than working out problems. To succeed in CHEN 204 with Dr. Mashuga, proficiency in self-teaching material is likely very necessary.

avoid if possible. lectures do not teach you the logic required to solve problems and he is not available unless by appointment. on the first exam the average was failing and only upon seeing a repeat performance on the second exam did he consider adding a curve. he does not like being emailed and will direct all questions to assistant prof and tas

CHEN 455 during Spring Semester. Prof Mashuga provides great lectures while tying in what takes place in both industry and his research lab. Homeworks and slides are very important for exams. 2 exams (includes final which is not cumulative) are open note, open slides, and open textbook. Should be able to find what you need in real time.
I loved this class, it teaches so many useful things and Dr. Mashuga is great about connecting everything to industry. If you do the homework's exams are easy and getting a good grade isn't to hard.
He is really good at bring things he has learned from industry into class. His exams are fair and he gives LOTS of partial credit. He is a prof you want to take for some class at some point.

I just want to clarify on the review below that he doesn't give partial credit to LATE homework, if it's late it's a zero. He gives plenty of partial credit on exams and homework. Also he has fun work stories !!

Loved this professor! He's very clear about his expectations and his exams are similar to the practice problems given in class. Although he doesn't give any partial credit,if your assignment's late it's a zero(I think it's his pet peeve).I liked listening to his lectures and it's clear he wants to see us succeed. We even took a class pic at the end

Professor Mashuga's lectures were easy to follow and his exams were not horribly difficult if you paid attention beforehand. The only issue I experienced in his class was lack of communication with students-- it was extremely difficult to get help for the term project and for other assignments in general.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is the most reasonable prof in the CHEN department. He allows nearly unlimited resources except the internet on tests to simulate solving problems in industry. His tests are pretty easy too. They usually follow examples that he's done in class. He is also pretty easy to talk to in office hours. He's hands down the best prof I've had in CHEN.

I'm sorry but he was not a good prof for our course this semester. Tried scheduling a meeting with him and it was impossible. Graded very harshly on the exams, and barely gave any partial credit even though there was plenty of work written down. Honestly, I would not take him again.

Dr. Mashuga is a great lecturer. He teaches beyond just passing the course. Lots of field examples. Want to get A? 1- attend his classes and listen carefully to his lecture. 2- study from his slides and rework all problems 3- understand your homework very, very well 4- develop a good equation sheet as you go His exams are open-book!
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had in CHEN. His teaching style is easier to follow even though the class is hard and he really knows how to relate to his students. He also gives a lot of partial credit and his tests are really similar to the examples in class. He also lets you use the ppt slides for the tests. Definitely recommend him

He has been one of my favorite profs in CHEN so far for this class. The tests are very fair although they are pretty short so you really have to know what you are doing. Everything on the tests will be covered in lectures so I definitely recommend attending because they are a lot of help.

One of the worst profs I've ever hard. This semester he left our class as an afterthought to his research and his other course. Barely gave any partial credit on exams, and many students complained about this and he got mad at us for questioning his grading methods. Honestly avoid him for 304, because he doesn't like it when people question him.
if you pay attention to his notes, his tests are pretty similar. plus he works out a ton of examples in class.

Chad was an amazing prof, his class was super organized. Lectures made sense, and the homework was not too hard but still very helpful for the exams. He was the best prof during covid season. I would absolutely take his class again.

I am very surprised to find the reviews I did on here for Dr. Mashuga. He is the best chemical engineering prof I have ever had so far, and is very intelligent when it comes to industry. He gives reviews, and he covers plenty of examples so preparing is a lot easier. in regards to the format of the online exam, IMO is more than fair.

I'm not sure how Dr. Mashuga conducted class before everything got switched to online, but the way he handles online exams are terrible - no partial credit, you cannot look back at any of the questions, and hard questions worth a large portion of the exam. He also seems very unsympathetic towards students who are worried about their grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: - the course is interesting but the professor makes it very difficult - he does not explain or make a good effort to clarify things, he basically skips through his slides like flipping through pages in a book - intentionally uses hard questions -has attitude issues
